doc.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG Tier List
doc.summary: The Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG tier list, updated November 3, 2026: Angelechy leads with no deck in Tier 1. Ranked from 75,365 YGO Omega ladder games.

infobox.caption: The most used card of Angelechy, the top deck

blocks.md: This Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG tier list ranks the strongest decks on the YGO Omega TCG ladder by their results, using data through November 2, 2026. No deck reaches Tier 1 this week; Angelechy leads.

blocks.caption: The TCG tier list at a glance

blocks.md: A tier here measures **how well a deck wins**, not how much it is played, and a small sample can't lift a deck to the top. For what moved this week, read the [latest meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-3-2026); for the other ladder, the [Genesys tier list](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-genesys-tier-list); for the numbers as they change, the [live statistics page](/statistics).

blocks.text: Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG tier list at a glance

blocks.md:
| | |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | None |
| Tier 1.5 | None |
| Tier 2 | Angelechy, Radiant Typhoon / Noble Knight, Dracotail / Branded, Artmage / Elfnote |
| Decks in the tiers | 16 |
| Games counted | 75,365 |
| Players | 5,348 |
| Going first wins | 57.8% of game 1 |
| Season opened | October 19, 2026 |
The TCG ladder is 15 days into the 10.2026 season, with 75,365 games from 5,348 players. The most played deck, Angelechy, holds 14.5% of the meta, and the 16 decks in these tiers cover 50% of it.

| Deck | Expected win rate | 95% interval | Meta share | Players |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Angelechy** | **53.3%** | 51.7–54.9 | 14.5% | 736 |
| **Radiant Typhoon / Noble Knight** | **53.1%** | 50.7–55.4 | 3.1% | 216 |
| **Dracotail / Branded** | **52.9%** | 49.8–56.0 | 0.6% | 77 |
| **Artmage / Elfnote** | **52.6%** | 51.1–54.0 | 9.2% | 497 |

Expected win rates here run from 52.6% (Artmage / Elfnote) to 53.3% (Angelechy).

blocks.text: Which decks are underplayed and overplayed?

blocks.md:
Popularity and results don't always agree. The underplayed decks reach Tier 2 or better on a small share of the meta, though the people playing them may be specialists, so treat them as leads to test. The overplayed decks are among the ten most played without reaching Tier 2.

- **Underplayed:** Dracotail / Branded (0.6% of the meta, expected 52.9%), Radiant Typhoon / Noble Knight (3.1% of the meta, expected 53.1%) and Artmage / Elfnote (9.2% of the meta, expected 52.6%)
- **Overplayed:** Elfnote / Artmage (8.3% of the meta, expected 52.4%), HERO (6.6% of the meta, expected 49.8%) and Blitzclique (4.9% of the meta, expected 51.7%)

Best and worst matchup for each top deck against Tiers 1 to 3. A matchup is listed only when its 95% interval excludes the rate the two decks' strengths predict, with at least 300 games.

| Deck | Best matchup | Worst matchup |
|---|---|---|
| **Angelechy** | **[Artmage / Elfnote, 52.5% (1,939 games)]{#4fdc8c}** | **[Radiant Typhoon / Noble Knight, 46.8% (663 games)]{#ff8594}** |
| **Radiant Typhoon / Noble Knight** | **[Angelechy, 53.2% (663 games)]{#4fdc8c}** | None clear |
| **Dracotail / Branded** | None clear | None clear |
| **Artmage / Elfnote** | None clear | **[Angelechy, 47.4% (1,939 games)]{#ff8594}** |
| **Elfnote / Artmage** | None clear | None clear |
| **Light and Darkness Ritual** | None clear | None clear |

Every number comes from ranked games played on [YGO Omega](/wiki/ygo-omega-wiki), the same data behind our [statistics page](/statistics). Nothing is voted on or picked by hand.

These are **power tiers**: they rank results, and the statistics page shows the same tiers.

**Each deck gets an expected win rate.** One model reads the games of the season between players rated Gold and up, after leaving out players with too few ranked games and one-off decklists: each deck has a strength, and the chance of winning depends on the two strengths, on who went first and on the rating gap. A deck's expected win rate is its strength against the whole field, weighted by how much each deck is played, and a deck with few games is pulled toward the middle. A tier reads that rate against fixed marks:

| Tier | Expected win rate |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 55% or more |
| Tier 1.5 | 54% or more |
| Tier 2 | 52.5% or more |
| Tier 3 | 51% or more |
| Tier 4 | 50% or more |

Decks under the last mark stay outside the tiers. A deck needs at least 0.5% of the meta and 10 players to be ranked at all, because the model corrects for few games, not for few pilots.

- **Meta share** is the deck's share of deck-games. Each game counts once per player, and mirror matches count.
- **The 95% interval** is the range the expected win rate is likely in, widened by how much the deck's daily results move beyond chance.
- **Decks** are grouped by the archetypes they run, so a hybrid counts apart from pure builds.

blocks.title: What this list can't tell you
blocks.md: This is ladder play on a simulator, not tournament results. Players of every level are in it, and a deck played mostly by specialists can score above what it would do in most hands. It shows what wins on the ladder, which is not always what wins a premier event.

items.q: What is the best TCG deck right now?
items.md: Angelechy, with an expected 53.3% win rate (95% interval 51.7–54.9) at 14.5% of the meta.

items.q: Is this tier list based on tournament results?
items.md: No. It comes from ranked ladder games on YGO Omega. That gives a far larger sample than tournaments, but it reflects ladder play, not premier events.
By expected win rate against the field: Tier 1 from 55%, Tier 1.5 from 54%, Tier 2 from 52.5%, Tier 3 from 51%, Tier 4 from 50%. Decks under 0.5% of the meta or 10 players aren't ranked.

items.q: Does a popular deck get a higher tier?
items.md: No. Tiers follow results. Elfnote / Artmage holds 8.3% of the meta and sits in Tier 3, while Dracotail / Branded holds 0.6% and sits in Tier 2.

items.q: How much does going first matter?
items.md: Going first wins 57.8% of game 1 between even decks on the TCG ladder.

items.q: How often is the tier list updated?
items.md: Every week, on this same page. Each week also gets its own [meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-november-3-2026), and the [statistics page](/statistics) shows the current numbers between updates.

items.q: Where can I see decklists for these decks?
items.md: The [statistics page](/statistics) has sample decklists, card usage and full matchup tables for each deck.
